title: Technology Sector Update for 09/06/2018: MDB,SEAC,CLDR,CUB - Nasdaq.com
text:

Technology stocks pared some of their earlier losses, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 Thursday losing just over 0.7% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was plunging more than 2.6%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) MongoDB ( MDB ) jumped to a record high on Thursday, rising almost 10% to top out at $79.11 a share after reporting a smaller--than-expected adjusted Q2 net loss and revenue exceeding analyst estimates. Excluding one-time items, the net loss for the database platform company during the three months ended Jan. 31 was $0.41 per share during the three months ended July 31 on $57.5 million in revenue, improving on a $0.52 per share adjusted loss during the year following a 61% increase in revenue over year-ago levels. Analysts, on average, had been expecting a $0.45 per share net loss for the three months ended July 31 on $51.75 million in revenue. It also is projecting Q3 and FY19 revenue exceeding Wall Street forecasts.
In other sector news:
(+) Cloudera ( CLDR ) raced as much as 23% higher on Thursday after reporting Q2 financial results exceeding Wall Street expectations and also issued Q3 and FY19 outlooks topping analyst projections, prompting analysts at Needham & Co Thursday to boost their price target for the machine learning and analytics company by $1 to $23 a share. Excluding one-time items, its adjusted net loss narrowed to $0.08 from $0.17 in the year-ago period and beating the Capital IQ consensus expecting a $0.15 per share non-GAAP net loss. Revenue climbed to $110.34 million from $89.83 million last year and also surpassing the $107.71 analyst mean.
(+) SeaChange International ( SEAC ) Thursday was more than 4% higher despite the television and video accessories company reporting a non-GAAP Q2 net loss of $0.18 per share for the three months ended July 31, missing the three-analyst consensus expecting breakeven earnings. Revenue fell to $11.9 million from $17.2 million last year but narrowly topping the $11.7 million analyst mean. It also projected Q3 financial results matching analyst estimates although its FY19 forecast lagged the Capital IQ consenus on both the top and bottom lines.
(+) Cubic ( CUB ) was back on positive ground Thursday afternoon, recovering from a fractional mid-morning decline, after saying its Cubic Mission Solutions division has received orders worth more than a combined $55 million to deliver its inflatable satellite communication and networking systems to the U.S. Army.
